comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences (Pedagogische wetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Current UU published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum describes a three-year bachelor. Its first year contains eight named block courses, and the coherent pathway assigns the standard 7.5 EC to each. The second year likewise uses eight 7.5-EC block slots; where block four presents Pedagogische Praktijkontwikkeling, onderzoek en beleid and Doing a qualitative research project as alternatives beside Test- en observatievaardigheden, the first-listed option is selected by official order. The official page states that one quarter of the degree is genuine profiling space, giving 45 EC, and places the thesis across the final two blocks; the thesis is recorded as 15 EC. The pathway therefore totals 120 EC in years one and two, a 15-EC thesis and 45 EC of open profiling space. No particular profiling elective, minor, stage or study-abroad option is invented.

alternatives.concept: Combines developmental and social psychology, cognition, family and school contexts, sociology, communication, ethics and empirical methods to study children and adolescents in the environments where they grow up. It is the closest feasible UCR response, while UCR lacks dedicated pedagogy, family-support practice, diagnostics and supervised clinical training.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Relative to the closest plan, this route replaces much of the sociology, communication and philosophy strand with biomedical foundations, public health, life science, ecology and advanced clinical-developmental psychology. Eleven courses differ, so the educational choice is substantially more health- and intervention-oriented.

alternatives.concept: Uses Utrecht's societal-pedagogy and youth-policy evidence to organise sociology, political institutions, law, economic policy, gender history, inclusion and resilience around how society supports children and families.

notes.text: Utrecht's programme is a dedicated Pedagogical Sciences degree with compulsory child-development pedagogy, diagnostics, intervention, professional communication, testing and observation, policy-oriented practice and a thesis. UCR can build strong developmental, psychological, social, ethical, policy and research foundations, but it does not reproduce the profession-specific pedagogical and supervised clinical-skills sequence.
